items.stem: An invoice field is extracted with a low confidence score. What is the most appropriate automated response?

options.text: Route that field to human review before it is accepted
options.rationale: Correct: low confidence should trigger review, not silent acceptance.
Accepting low-confidence data risks propagating errors.
Discarding wastes correct fields; only the uncertain field needs review.

options.text: Re-run the same processor until confidence rises
options.rationale: Re-running the same processor on the same input does not change the result.

items.explanation: Correct: low confidence should trigger review, not silent acceptance.

items.stem: Which TWO steps are needed to report extraction accuracy honestly? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Compare extracted fields to a labelled ground-truth sample
options.rationale: Correct: accuracy requires a known-correct reference.

options.text: Report accuracy per field type, not just an overall number
options.rationale: Correct: per-field reporting exposes weak fields.

options.text: Assume accuracy equals the average confidence score
options.rationale: Confidence is not the same as measured accuracy.

options.text: Test only on documents the processor was tuned with

items.explanation: Correct: both keyed options are right; the distractors are wrong for the reasons given.

items.stem: You need to extract vendor, date and totals from standard invoices. Which processor choice is best?

options.rationale: Correct: a specialized parser targets invoice entities directly.
OCR returns text but not structured invoice entities.

options.text: A form-field processor for a different document type
options.rationale: A mismatched processor extracts the wrong fields.

options.text: No processor; parse the PDF with string matching
options.rationale: Manual string matching is brittle and error-prone.
